notes.decision: Rendered 'which defiles.' I read ⲭⲁⲍⲙⲉ as a Lycopolitan variant of Sahidic ϫⲱϩⲙ ('defile, pollute'), with ϫ→ⲭ and ϩ→ⲍ both attested in this dialect. The subject (likely Sin or her body, continuing from p.95) defiles those it gathers in. An alternative would be Greek χάσμα ('chasm/abyss'), but no verbal sense fits.

Rendered tentatively as 'those who are in want.' Read as Lycopolitan equivalent of Sahidic ⲟⲉⲓⲧ ('to be needy, in want, lack'), giving 'the needy ones.' Alternatives considered: (1) ⲱⲁⲧ 'thick, dense'; (2) a form of ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲉ 'be wrapped.' The 'in want' reading fits Manichaean discourse about souls trapped in matter.

Rendered 'she has clothed (herself) with Error and Forgetfulness.' ⲣ̄-ⲫⲟⲣⲉ from Greek φορεῖν ('to wear'). ⲧⲃⲱⲉ = ⲧⲃϣⲉ/ⲃϣⲉ 'forgetfulness.' Both Error (ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ) and Forgetfulness are standard Manichaean cosmic personifications, hence capitalized.

Rendered 'she has stamped/sealed.' Reading ⲣ̄-ⲡ-ⲧⲱⲃⲱ as 'make the seal/imprint of,' from ⲧⲱⲃⲉ ('seal, stamp, mold'). The image is of Sin imprinting her own character on her substance, kind, and form. Alternatives: 'recompense' (ⲧⲱⲃⲉ also = 'requite') or 'transform/exchange.' Settled on 'stamp' as preserving the concrete image of the verbal root.
Rendered 'her form/shape.' ⲣⲉⲓⲧⲉ/ⲣⲏⲧⲉ in Coptic = 'manner, kind, form.' Together with ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ (substance) and ⲅⲉⲛⲟⲥ (kind) it makes a triad of essence-categories.

Rendered 'the place of ascent.' ⲙⲁⲛ- = 'place of'; ⲱⲩⲗⲏⲩ I read as a verbal noun from ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲉ/ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲥ-type root meaning 'go up, climb, ascend.' Sin does not know the door leading upward — i.e., the way of escape from the body. Reading uncertain; could also relate to ⲟⲩⲗⲗⲱ ('shelter') or another root.
Rendered 'to keep watch; she calls out.' ⲁⲣⲁϩ = ⲁⲣⲉϩ 'guard, keep'; ⲥ-ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ '(she) calls.' Punctuation and clause boundaries here are uncertain due to surrounding lacunae.
Rendered 'against him.' Lycopolitan equivalent of Sahidic ⲉϩⲣⲁⲓ̈ ⲟⲩⲃⲏϥ ('upward against him'). The ⲍ- = ϩ- and -ⲃⲏϩ = -ⲃⲏϥ are standard Lyco substitutions.
Rendered 'she became an enemy to her father.' ⲣ̄-ⲭⲁⲭⲉ = 'become enemy.' This casts Sin as having turned hostile to her own progenitor — a classic Manichaean motif.
Rendered 'being evil/bad.' ⲍⲁⲩ = Sahidic ϩⲟⲟⲩ 'bad, evil' in stative.

Rendered '[the mind of] light which is in the soul.' Following Gardner's reconstruction; the structure introduces the mind-of-light embedded in the soul, which is then released faculty by faculty in lines 13-21.

Rendered 'he raises.' ϣⲁ- (habitual/aorist) + ϩ (3ms) + ⲧⲟⲩⲱ ('raise'). Per terminology guidelines, ⲧⲟⲩⲱ must preserve vertical/directional semantics. The Savior raises each faculty up out of its bodily prison.

The pattern: 'he releases (ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) the [faculty] of the soul from the [body element], binding (ⲙⲟⲩⲣ) the [faculty] also of Sin in the [body element].' This is the central soteriological diagram of the page. Note interesting variation: L13-14 'raises the mind from the bone' (ⲧⲟⲩⲱ), but L14ff use 'release' (ⲃⲱⲗ) — both senses are operative, soul going up and binding going down.
Rendered 'the bone' and 'the sinew.' ⲡⲕⲉⲥ = Sahidic ⲕⲁⲥ 'bone'; ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲧ = 'sinew, nerve.' The five-element body schema (bone/sinew/vein/flesh/skin) is standard Manichaean anthropology.
Rendered 'the vein.' ⲙⲟⲟⲙⲉ in Coptic = 'vein, blood-vessel.'
Rendered 'the skin.' ϣⲁⲁⲣ/ϣⲁⲁⲣⲉ = 'skin, hide' in Coptic.
Rendered 'also.' Lycopolitan ⲍⲱⲱϩ = Sahidic ϩⲱⲱϥ ('also, in turn, for his/its part'). Marks the parallel binding of Sin's faculty corresponding to each soul-faculty being released.
Rendered 'freeing them' (lit. 'making them free'). ⲣⲙ̄ⲍⲉ = Sahidic ⲣⲙ̄ϩⲉ 'free person, freedom'; with ⲉⲣ̄- 'become free' / cause to become free.
Rendered 'which had been loosed.' Stative ⲃⲏⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ from ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('release') — Sin's five members had previously been let loose (in the body's formation), and now the Savior re-binds them.

Rendered tentatively 'weaves them together.' From ⲥⲁϩⲧ/ⲥⲱϩⲧ̄ — Crum gives 'weave' for ⲥⲁϩⲧ. The image of weaving fits the construction of the New Man as a kind of garment/tissue. Alternatives: 'make ready, prepare, set up firm' (also given for ⲥⲱϩⲧ̄), or 'select' (if reading as ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄, which would require dialectal substitution). 'Weave' chosen for its concrete imagistic force in the Manichaean cosmogonic context.
Rendered 'a New Man.' Compound ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲛ- + ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ ('new'). Standard Manichaean term for the regenerated person.
Rendered 'Righteousness.' Greek loanword δικαιοσύνη. Capitalized as a personified/cosmic principle (the New Man is its son).

Rendered 'the time, however, when he is about to mold him, and to fashion and to select the New Man.' ⲙⲟⲩⲟⲩⲛⲕ = ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲅ 'mold, form, fashion'; ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ = ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'establish, prepare'; ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ = ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose, select.' Three coordinated verbs of demiurgic shaping.
Rendered 'he brings forth.' ⲭⲡⲁ = Lycopolitan form of ϫⲡⲟ ('beget, produce, bring forth'). The Savior generates the five new living members from the five (now-bound) Sin-members.
Rendered 'great living members.' ⲛⲁⲟ = Lyco for ⲛⲟϭ 'great'; ⲁⲛⲍ̄ = ⲟⲛϩ 'alive, living.' These contrast with the dead/sin-bound members.
Rendered 'the love.' Greek loanword ἀγάπη. The mind of the New Man is identified with love (rather than mere intellect) — a striking equation typical of Manichaean ethics.
Rendered 'the faith.' ⲛⲁⲍⲧⲉ = Lycopolitan ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ ('faith, trust'). The thought of the New Man = faith.

Rendered '[the perfection].' ⲭⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('completion, perfection') is Gardner's restoration based on the parallel structure (love–faith–X) and on standard Manichaean triads. The teaching of the New Man = perfection. The restoration is highly probable given the formula.

Rendered tentatively as a relative clause referring back to the New Man whom 'he weaves.' The grammatical seam between this and 'the teaching' is awkward; the text may intend 'and the (mind/thought) which he weaves with the teaching.' Reading uncertain.

proposed_terms.rationale: Lycopolitan ⲡⲕⲉⲥ = Sahidic ⲕⲁⲥ 'bone.' First member of the five-element body system in the Kephalaia anthropology (bone/sinew/vein/flesh/skin), correlated to mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection respectively.
Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲧ = 'sinew, nerve.' Second of the five body elements; correlated to thought.
Coptic ⲙⲟⲟⲙⲉ = 'vein, vessel.' Third of the five body elements; correlated to teaching.
Coptic ϣⲁⲁⲣ/ϣⲁⲣⲉ = 'skin, hide.' Fifth of the five body elements; correlated to reflection.

Compound: ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ ('new'). Standard Manichaean term for the regenerated soul-body that the Savior fashions, son of Righteousness, with five living members corresponding to love, faith, perfection (and presumably two more in the lacuna). Equivalent to Pauline καινὸς ἄνθρωπος adopted into Manichaean technical vocabulary.

ϫⲱⲕ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ literally 'completion outward' — to bring to fullness, accomplish. As the noun-virtue identified with the teaching-faculty of the New Man, 'perfection' captures the technical sense (cf. Greek τελείωσις).
Lycopolitan form of Sahidic ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'faith, trust, belief.' Identified here with the thought-faculty of the New Man.

Most likely from ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, stamp, mold,' with light verb ⲣ̄- ('do, make'). 'She stamps her substance and her kind and her form' — Sin imprints her character upon her own essence-categories. Alternative: ⲧⲱⲃⲉ also = 'requite, recompense,' but that fits less well here. Reading remains uncertain; flagged in footnote.

Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲱⲩⲗⲏⲩ, tentatively read as a verbal noun from a root meaning 'go up, ascend' (cf. ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲉ, ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲥ). Sin does not know 'the door of the place of ascent' — the way out and up. The reading is tentative.

translation:
[L1] [Sin,] which defiles, which gathers those who are in want{1} in their likenesses and their [L2] forms — she has clothed (herself) with Error and Forgetfulness; she has stamped{2} [L3] her substance and her kind and her form, not [L4] knowing the door of the place of ascent,{3} so as to keep watch; she calls out{4} [L5] against him; she became an enemy to her father [...] [L6] [...] her, being evil [...] [L7] [...] to her light alone, [...] [the mind of] [L8] light which is in the soul [...] [L9] [...] she clothes (it) with it in the [...] [L10] [...] her wisdom [...] [L11] [...] she [...] for her [...] [L12] [...] with bonds [...]

[L13] members in the body. He raises the [mind of the soul, releasing][L14] it from the bone. He releases the [thought of the soul] [L15] from the sinew, binding the thought also [of Sin in] [L16] the sinew. He releases the teaching of the soul from the vein, [L17] binding the teaching also of Sin in the vein. He [L18] raises the counsel of the soul, releasing it from the flesh, [L19] binding the counsel also of Sin in the flesh. He [L20] releases the reflection of the soul from the skin, binding [L21] the reflection of Sin in the skin.

[L22] In this way, then, he releases the members of the soul, [L23] freeing them from the five members of Sin. [L24] These five members of Sin, which had been loosed,{5} [L25] he binds them. He establishes the members of the soul; he places them, [L26] he weaves them together,{6} he establishes them as a New Man, a son [L27] of Righteousness. The time, however, [when] he is about to mold him, [L28] and to fashion and to select the New Man — then he brings forth the five [L29] living members out of the five members [L30] and places them in the members of the New Man. He places the [mind], [L31] which is the love, in the mind of the New Man. The thought [L32] also, which is the faith, he places [it in] the thought [of the New] [L33] Man, which he weaves(?). The teaching, which is [the perfection,{7} he places it in the teaching of the New Man...]
